Rotation (Rodrigues’ rotation formula) If the original structure has the normal vector (or the axis) in the z-direction; it is so rotated that the normal vector now becomes [nx ny nz]

engines.mesh.mesh_rotate2 module¶

engines.mesh.mesh_rotate2.mesh_rotate2(P=None, axis=None, theta=None)[source]¶

SYNTAX P = meshrotate2(P, axis, theta) DESCRIPTION This function implements rotation (Rodrigues’ rotation formula) of the mesh about an axis with vector ‘axis’. Rotation angle is to be given in radians.

To display the mesh use: fv.faces = t; fv.vertices = P; patch(fv, ‘FaceColor’, ‘y’); axis equal; view(160, 60); grid on;

Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Modeling for Electrical and Biological Systems Using MATLAB, Sergey N. Makarov, Gregory M. Noetscher, and Ara Nazarian, Wiley, New York, 2015, 1st ed.

engines.mesh.mesh_tri module¶

engines.mesh.mesh_tri.mesh_tri(arg1, arg2=None)[source]¶

This function creates integration points and weights for triangles

Syntax: [coeff, weights, IndexF] = mesh_tri(3) - will do barycentric subdivision with

3*3 = 9 integration points

[coeff, weights, IndexF] = mesh_tri(7,5) - will use Gaussian quadrature of fifth

order with seven integration points

Description: Uses Gaussian quadratures (with authors permission) from http://www.cs.kuleuven.ac.be/~nines/research/ecf/ecf.html Formulas of third (4 integration points), fifth (7 integration points) seventh (13 integration points), and tenth (25 integration points) order of accuracy may be created

Uses the “edge” method for barycentric subdivision of arbitrary order, where the edges of smaller triangles (similar to the original one) are equally subdivided. This gives the desired barycentric points.

Copyright SNM 2002-2020 SP 2026

engines.mesh.meshplaneint_axis_nonmanifold module¶

engines.mesh.meshplaneint_axis_nonmanifold.meshplaneint_axis_nonmanifold(P: ndarray, t: ndarray, axis: int, val: float, tol: float = 1e-09, compTri: ndarray | None = None, opts: dict | None = None) → tuple[ndarray, ndarray, ndarray, ndarray | None, bool, float][source]¶

Intersect a (possibly non-manifold) triangle mesh with an axis-aligned plane P[:, axis-1] = val (axis 1->x, 2->y, 3->z).

Inputs¶

P : (Np, 3) vertices t : (Nt, 3) triangles, 0-based indices axis : 1, 2, or 3 val : plane coordinate value tol : point-uniqueness tolerance (default 1e-9) compTri : (Nt,) compartment label per triangle opts : dict with optional keys

shiftVal bool (default True) maxShiftIters int (default 20) degenerateMode str ‘first2’ | ‘skip’ (default ‘first2’)

Outputs¶

Pi : (Ni, 3) unique intersection points edgesI : (Ne, 2) segment endpoint indices into Pi ti : (Ne,) source triangle index per segment ci : (Ne,) compartment label per segment, or None flag : True if any segments were found valOut : final plane value used (may be shifted)
